title: Constructive first-order quantifier laws and their limits

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Syntax and semantics of predicate logic; Natural Deduction (handout 8)

summary: Derive constructive quantifier laws and distinguish them from stronger classical shifts using growing domains and an infinite chain of stages.
abstract: A proof that every object has one of two properties need not decide which property all objects share. We derive the quantifier distributions and implication shifts that constructive deduction does permit, including the exact conditions on independent formulas and witness branches. Explicit models then separate those laws from stronger principles: growing domains refute the constant-domain schema, while an infinite chain makes every object eventually satisfy a predicate without ever verifying its universal claim. The same chain gives a classical quantified theorem whose double negation has no intuitionistic proof, marking the boundary of the propositional Glivenko theorem.
